newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Turning higher with T-bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Turning higher with T-bonds.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds, which had opened flat, gained about a quarter of a point in early afternoon trade on Tuesday, primarily reflecting the strength of the Treasury market.

"With the release of the National Association of Purchasing Management index and the Leading Indicators, the market ticked up, I would say a solid one-quarter of a point on the long-end," a trader said.

The June NAPM report showed the U.S. manufacturing sector was growing at a brisk pace, while inventories appeared to be contracting, the chairman of the association's business committee said. The index slipped to 55.7 percent last month, from 57.1 percent in May. A reading below 50 suggests the ecoonomy is contracting, while one above signals growth.
May Leading Indicators rose 0.3 percent in May, snapping back from April's 0.1 percent downturn, according to the Conference Board.

New municipal issues sold this week appeared to be selling fairly smoothly, even though traders said the market was a bit subdued as a number of players were taking the entire week off in order to take advantage of the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday.

"Frankly, all the new issues that have come and freed up ove the last couple of days seem relatively well-placed," a trader said, citing recent sales by a Philadelphia airport and a Detroit authority.
Tuesday's sales included a $140.5 million offering of bonds by Mississippi, which was won by Goldman, Sachs at 5.188 percent true interest cost.
In the secondary market, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, Sanitary Authority of 2024, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.63 percent, NET, down three basis points.
And Detroit, Michigan, Sewer Disposal Revenues of 2022, which pay a five percent coupon, were offered at 5.53 percent, NET, down two basis points.
September municipal bond futures gained 19 ticks to 117-3/32, while September Treasury bonds rose 20 ticks to 111-22/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 172 ticks.
